newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: SFE wheat continues strong rise on short covering.
newsitem.headline: SFE wheat continues strong rise on short covering.

text.p: Sydney Futures Exchange (SFE) wheat futures again rose strongly on Wednesday on good volume.
A total of 51 contracts were traded, with traded prices increasing by A$5.50 and A$6.50 a tonne.
January 1998 firmed A$5.50 to A$197.50, while March 1998 rose A$6.50 to A$200.00 a tonne.
Settlement prices in untraded contracts also rose by similar amounts.
The strong market rise followed a firmer U.S. market, which saw a technical break on good volume and fresh export sales to Egypt, one broker said.
Locally, the upward move reflected short-covering and good end user demand amid on-going concern at the lack of rain in some areas and a possible El Nino effect.
"A number of things are all coming together to drive the local market sharply higher," the broker said.
Interest in option trade had also picked up substantially in line with the rise in wheat futures prices, he added.
